es: Identificar la tesis, las razones y los ejemplos de un párrafo de opinión sobre la vida escolar y ordenar sus frases.

teaching.en: My claim is that schools should start later.
teaching.es: Mi tesis es que las clases deberían empezar más tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim = lo que defiendes; en una frase, suele ir al principio del párrafo.
segments: My claim is that
schools should start later.
teaching.audioText: My claim is that schools should start later.

teaching.en: My first reason is that teenagers need more sleep.
teaching.es: Mi primera razón es que los adolescentes necesitan dormir más.
teaching.explanationEs: Reason = por qué defiendes la tesis.
segments: My first reason is that
teenagers need more sleep.
teaching.audioText: My first reason is that teenagers need more sleep.

teaching.en: For example, many students fall asleep in the first lesson.
teaching.es: Por ejemplo, muchos estudiantes se duermen en la primera clase.
teaching.explanationEs: Example = un caso real que hace creíble la razón; for example va al inicio de la frase.
segments: For example, many students fall
asleep in the first lesson.
teaching.audioText: For example, many students fall asleep in the first lesson.

teaching.en: A fact or a number is stronger evidence than a feeling.
teaching.es: Un dato o una cifra es una prueba más fuerte que una sensación.
teaching.explanationEs: Fact = dato comprobable; evidence = lo que demuestra que la razón es cierta.
segments: A fact or a number is
stronger evidence than a feeling.
teaching.audioText: A fact or a number is stronger evidence than a feeling.

teaching.en: To argue well, a writer makes sure that every reason supports the claim.
teaching.es: Para argumentar bien, quien escribe se asegura de que cada razón respalde la tesis.
teaching.explanationEs: Support = respaldar: una razón que no apoya la tesis cambia de tema.
segments: To argue well, a writer makes sure
that every reason supports the claim.
teaching.audioText: To argue well, a writer makes sure that every reason supports the claim.

teaching.en: A clear paragraph can end with a short conclusion that repeats the claim.
teaching.es: Un párrafo claro puede terminar con una conclusión breve que repite la tesis.
teaching.explanationEs: Conclusion = cierre que recuerda la tesis con otras palabras.
segments: A clear paragraph can end with a
short conclusion that repeats the claim.
teaching.audioText: A clear paragraph can end with a short conclusion that repeats the claim.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la tesis de este párrafo?

choices.text: Students need time for sports.
Schools should have a shorter day.
My brother plays football only on Sundays.

feedback.es: La tesis es lo que defiende el autor; las otras dos frases dan la razón y un caso concreto.

hint.es: La tesis es lo que el autor defiende; las demás frases la apoyan.

origin.text: Schools should have a shorter day. Students need time for sports. For example, my brother plays football only on Sundays.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase del párrafo es la razón?

choices.text: The school should sell fruit.
Mia feels more awake after an apple.
Fruit is healthier than cake.

feedback.es: La razón explica por qué: la fruta es más sana que el pastel. La primera frase es la tesis y la última, un ejemplo.

hint.es: Busca la frase que explica por qué se defiende la tesis.

origin.text: The school should sell fruit. Fruit is healthier than cake. For example, Mia feels more awake after an apple.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por ejemplo, muchos estudiantes llegan tarde.»

answer.text: For

feedback.es: El ejemplo se introduce con for example, o con for instance.

hint.es: Es la preposición con la que empieza la expresión.

origin.text: ___ example, many students arrive late.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función en el párrafo.

pairs: A uniform saves time in the morning.
For example, Leo gets dressed in two minutes.
So a uniform is a practical choice.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función: la tesis defiende, la razón explica, el ejemplo muestra un caso y la conclusión cierra.

pairs: A uniform saves time in the morning.
For example, Leo gets dressed in two minutes.
So a uniform is a practical choice.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ejemplo da la persona.

choices.text: A student who studies in a noisy place.
A student who has a private room.
A student who studies at school.

feedback.es: El ejemplo es el caso de Leo, que estudia en la cocina mientras sus hermanos juegan: un lugar ruidoso.

origin.audio: I think the library should open on Saturdays. Many students have no quiet place at home. For instance, Leo studies in the kitchen while his brothers play.

prompt.es: ¿Qué orden de frases forma un párrafo lógico?

choices.text: a – b – c
b – c – a
a – c – b

feedback.es: Primero va la tesis (b), después la razón (c) y por último el ejemplo (a) que la respalda. Un párrafo no puede empezar con For example, porque un ejemplo necesita algo que ilustrar.

origin.text: (a) For example, Sara gets home at six and has two hours of homework. (b) Homework should be shorter. (c) Students are tired in the evening.

prompt.es: ¿Qué orden de frases forma el párrafo más lógico?

choices.text: b – c – d – e – a
d – b – c – a – e
b – d – c – e – a

feedback.es: El párrafo empieza con la tesis (b), sigue con la razón (d), da el ejemplo (c) con su consecuencia (e) y cierra con la conclusión (a).

origin.text: (a) So a longer break would help everyone. (b) The lunch break should be longer. (c) For example, on Fridays only half the students finish their lunch. (d) Students need time to eat and to rest. (e) Many of them leave hungry.

prompt.es: ¿Qué función cumple la última frase de este párrafo?

choices.text: It gives an example.
It gives the claim.
It gives a reason.

feedback.es: La última frase cuenta un caso concreto (el primo que estudió todo el domingo): es un ejemplo.

origin.text: Students should not have a test on Monday. Weekends are the only time to rest. For instance, my cousin studied all Sunday and was tired on Monday.

prompt.es: Etiqueta cada frase del párrafo con la palabra que falta.

answer.text: claim | reason | example

feedback.es: La primera frase defiende (claim), la segunda explica por qué (reason) y la última da un caso (example).

origin.text: Uniforms should be free. Families already pay for books and trips. For example, my aunt paid sixty dollars for one trip.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué le falta al párrafo de la persona.

choices.text: A claim to argue.
A case that supports the reason.
A reason to explain the claim.

feedback.es: La persona tiene tesis y razón, pero dice que aún no tiene ejemplo: le falta un caso que respalde la razón.

origin.audio: My claim is that gym class should be every day. My reason is that students sit for hours. I have no example yet, so my paragraph is weak.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es una razón general y no un ejemplo concreto?

choices.text: Last Monday, Mia remembered the whole lesson after eight hours of sleep.
For instance, Tom slept well and passed the test.
Sleep helps us remember what we learn.

feedback.es: La razón es una idea general que explica; las otras dos frases cuentan casos concretos de personas, es decir, ejemplos.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La excursión debe ser en primavera porque hace mejor tiempo.»

answer.text: The trip should be in spring because the weather is better
accepted: The trip should be in spring because the weather is better
Because the weather is better, the trip should be in spring

feedback.es: Primero va la tesis (the trip should be in spring) y después la razón con because.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mi tesis es que los deberes deben ser más cortos.»

answer.text: claim

feedback.es: La tesis (claim) es la afirmación que defiende el autor.

origin.text: My ___ is that homework should be shorter.

title.en: In view of, on the grounds that
title.es: En vista de y con el argumento de

es: Justificar afirmaciones con in view of, on the grounds that, insofar as y seeing that eligiendo el conector y la estructura correctos.

teaching.en: In view of the noise, the school should close the road.
teaching.es: Dado el ruido, el colegio debería cerrar la calle.
teaching.explanationEs: In view of + sustantivo (the noise): fundamento que todos conocen; con una oración se dice in view of the fact that.
segments: In view of the noise, the
school should close the road.
teaching.audioText: In view of the noise, the school should close the road.

teaching.en: The school decided to ban phones on the grounds that they distract students.
teaching.es: El colegio decidió prohibir los móviles alegando que distraen a los estudiantes.
teaching.explanationEs: On the grounds that + oración completa: el motivo oficial de una decisión.
segments: The school decided to ban phones on
the grounds that they distract students.
teaching.audioText: The school decided to ban phones on the grounds that they distract students.

teaching.en: Homework is useful insofar as it helps students practise.
teaching.es: Los deberes son útiles en la medida en que ayudan a los estudiantes a practicar.
teaching.explanationEs: Insofar as + oración: la afirmación vale solo hasta cierto punto.
segments: Homework is useful insofar as
it helps students practise.
teaching.audioText: Homework is useful insofar as it helps students practise.

teaching.en: Seeing that the test is on Friday, we should revise tonight.
teaching.es: Visto que el examen es el viernes, deberíamos repasar esta noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Seeing that + oración: el motivo ya es conocido; suena más conversacional.
segments: Seeing that the test is on
Friday, we should revise tonight.
teaching.audioText: Seeing that the test is on Friday, we should revise tonight.

teaching.en: You need to justify a rule before you ask people to follow it.
teaching.es: Tienes que justificar una norma antes de pedir a la gente que la cumpla.
teaching.explanationEs: Justify = dar fundamento; estos conectores sirven para eso.
segments: You need to justify a rule before
you ask people to follow it.
teaching.audioText: You need to justify a rule before you ask people to follow it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué conector encaja con el sustantivo para justificar el cambio de aula?

choices.text: On the grounds that
Insofar as
In view of

feedback.es: Con un sustantivo (the noise) se usa in view of; los otros conectores necesitan una oración completa detrás.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que viene después del hueco: un sustantivo, no una oración.

origin.text: ___ the noise, we moved the class to the library.

prompt.es: Completa: «El colegio prohibió la comida en clase alegando que ensucia el suelo.»

answer.text: grounds

feedback.es: El motivo oficial de una decisión se introduce con on the grounds that + oración.

hint.es: Es el motivo oficial: on the ... that.

origin.text: The school banned food in class on the ___ that it makes the floor dirty.

prompt.es: ¿Qué conector limita la utilidad de los deberes a una condición?

choices.text: insofar as
in view of
seeing that

feedback.es: Insofar as significa «en la medida en que»: los deberes son útiles solo si cumplen la condición.

hint.es: Busca el conector que significa «en la medida en que».

origin.text: Homework is useful ___ it helps students practise.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Visto que llueve, deberíamos quedarnos dentro.»

answer.text: Seeing that it is raining, we should stay inside
accepted: Seeing that it is raining, we should stay inside
We should stay inside, seeing that it is raining

feedback.es: Seeing that va seguido de una oración completa (it is raining); después se escribe la consecuencia.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el fundamento con el que el colegio cerró el gimnasio.

choices.text: The gym was too old.
The weather was too hot.
The students were on holiday.

feedback.es: El director da el fundamento del cierre: hacía demasiado calor para hacer deporte por la tarde.

origin.audio: The school closed the gym because of the heat. The director said it was dangerous to play sport in the afternoon.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada comienzo de frase con su traducción.

pairs: On the grounds that it is unfair,

pairs.es: En la medida en que nos ayuda,

feedback.es: Cada conector tiene su equivalente: dado, alegando que, en la medida en que y visto que.

pairs: On the grounds that it is unfair,

pairs.es: En la medida en que nos ayuda,

prompt.es: Completa cada argumento con el conector de fundamento adecuado.

answer.text: In view of | on the grounds | insofar as | Seeing
accepted: In view of | on the grounds | insofar as | Seeing

feedback.es: Sustantivo: in view of; motivo de una decisión: on the grounds that (también encaja seeing that); condición: insofar as; motivo ya conocido: seeing that.

sentences: ___ the heavy rain, the match was cancelled.
The club refused the plan ___ that it cost too much.
Exercise is good for you ___ it is regular.
___ that everyone is here, let us start.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase usa bien el conector de fundamento?

choices.text: In view of the meeting was delayed, it was moved to Friday.
In view of that delayed the meeting, it was moved to Friday.
In view of the delay, the meeting was moved to Friday.

feedback.es: In view of va con un sustantivo (the delay). Las otras versiones lo usan con una oración y resultan incorrectas.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué condición pone la profesora a los deberes.

choices.text: Homework is fine only when it is short.
Homework is never fine.
Homework is fine when it is very long.

feedback.es: Insofar as it is short significa que los deberes valen solo en la medida en que sean breves.

origin.audio: The teacher said that homework is fine insofar as it is short. She also said that, seeing that the test is on Monday, there will be no homework this weekend.

prompt.es: Justifica con un conector de fundamento el cierre de la biblioteca los domingos.

answer.text: The library will close on Sundays on the grounds that there are few visitors.
accepted: The library will close on Sundays on the grounds that there are few visitors.
In view of the fact that few people visit it, the library will close on Sundays.
Seeing that there are few visitors, the library will close on Sundays.
In view of the low number of visitors, the library will close on Sundays.

feedback.es: Un conector de fundamento (on the grounds that, seeing that o in view of the fact that) introduce el motivo con una oración completa.

origin.text: Datos: la biblioteca cerrará los domingos; motivo: hay pocos visitantes.

evidenceGroups: in view of the fact that

prompt.es: ¿Qué conector introduce el motivo oficial de la decisión?

choices.text: in view of
on the grounds that
insofar as

feedback.es: El motivo oficial va con on the grounds that + oración completa (the roof needed repair).

prompt.es: Ordena: «Las reglas son justas en la medida en que todos las siguen.»

answer.text: Rules are fair insofar as everyone follows them
accepted: Rules are fair insofar as everyone follows them
Insofar as everyone follows them, rules are fair

feedback.es: Insofar as se escribe después de la afirmación y va seguido de una oración completa (everyone follows them).

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase está mal construida?

choices.text: In view of the late hour, we should leave.
Seeing that it is late, we should leave.
In view of it is late, we should leave.

feedback.es: In view of no puede ir seguido de una oración (it is late). Se corrige con un sustantivo o con seeing that + oración.

es: Detectar generalizaciones apresuradas, falsas causas y ataques a la persona en argumentos breves y elegir una réplica razonable.

teaching.en: A hasty generalisation takes one or two cases and turns them into a rule for everyone.
teaching.es: Una generalización apresurada toma uno o dos casos y los convierte en una regla para todos.
teaching.explanationEs: Hasty = sin pensar lo suficiente; generalisation = de pocos casos a una regla general.
segments: A hasty generalisation takes one or two cases
and turns them into a rule for everyone.
teaching.audioText: A hasty generalisation takes one or two cases and turns them into a rule for everyone.

teaching.en: The team lost after the new rule, but that may be a coincidence, not a cause.
teaching.es: El equipo perdió tras la nueva norma, pero eso puede ser una casualidad, no una causa.
teaching.explanationEs: Falsa causa: que algo ocurra después no significa que sea por eso.
segments: The team lost after the new rule, but
that may be a coincidence, not a cause.
teaching.audioText: The team lost after the new rule, but that may be a coincidence, not a cause.

teaching.en: Saying that Tom is wrong because he is always late is a personal attack, not an answer.
teaching.es: Decir que Tom se equivoca porque siempre llega tarde es un ataque personal, no una respuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Personal attack = criticar a quien habla en vez de a lo que dice.
segments: Saying that Tom is wrong because he is always
late is a personal attack, not an answer.
teaching.audioText: Saying that Tom is wrong because he is always late is a personal attack, not an answer.

teaching.en: A weak argument has a flaw: the reason does not really support the claim.
teaching.es: Un argumento débil tiene un fallo: la razón no respalda de verdad la tesis.
teaching.explanationEs: Flaw = el punto exacto donde falla el argumento.
segments: A weak argument has a flaw: the
reason does not really support the claim.
teaching.audioText: A weak argument has a flaw: the reason does not really support the claim.

teaching.en: A sample of two students is too small to prove a rule.
teaching.es: Una muestra de dos estudiantes es demasiado pequeña para probar una regla.
teaching.explanationEs: Sample = el grupo de casos que se estudia para sacar una conclusión.
segments: A sample of two students is
too small to prove a rule.
teaching.audioText: A sample of two students is too small to prove a rule.

teaching.en: A reasonable reply names the flaw and asks for better evidence.
teaching.es: Una réplica razonable nombra el fallo y pide mejores pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: Reply = respuesta a un argumento; se centra en la idea, no en la persona.
segments: A reasonable reply names the flaw
and asks for better evidence.
teaching.audioText: A reasonable reply names the flaw and asks for better evidence.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es el fallo de este argumento?

choices.text: A coincidence is taken as a cause.
One case becomes a general rule.
The speaker attacks a person.

feedback.es: Que el equipo perdiera el día de las zapatillas nuevas no prueba que ellas fueran la causa: es una falsa causa.

hint.es: Mira si algo que ocurre después se toma como causa.

origin.text: Our team lost on the day Leo wore new shoes, so the shoes made us lose.

prompt.es: ¿Qué réplica es razonable ante este argumento?

choices.text: You are not a good student either.
That is only two cases; we need a bigger sample.
I agree, so phones should be banned.

feedback.es: La réplica razonable nombra el fallo (solo dos casos) y pide una muestra mayor, sin atacar a la persona.

hint.es: Una réplica razonable nombra el fallo y pide más pruebas.

origin.text: Two students in my class use phones and got bad grades, so phones give everyone bad grades.

prompt.es: Completa: «Dos casos no son una muestra suficiente.»

answer.text: sample

feedback.es: Un sample es el grupo de casos que se estudia; dos casos son demasiado pocos para sacar una regla.

hint.es: Es el grupo de casos que se estudia para sacar una conclusión.

origin.text: Two cases are not a big enough ___.

prompt.es: ¿Qué fallo tiene este argumento?

choices.text: It takes one case as a rule.
It mixes up a coincidence and a cause.
It attacks the person, not the idea.

feedback.es: El hablante no responde a la idea sobre los uniformes: critica a la persona por llegar tarde.

origin.text: You cannot talk about school uniforms. You always arrive late.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué fallo tiene el argumento.

choices.text: It draws a general rule from two cases.
It attacks the owner of the shops.
It says one event caused another.

feedback.es: Del caso de dos tiendas se saca una regla para todas: es una generalización apresurada.

origin.audio: I visited two shops in the town. Both were closed on Monday. So all the shops in the town are closed on Monday.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Eso es solo un caso, así que necesitamos más pruebas.»

answer.text: That is only one case, so we need more evidence

feedback.es: La réplica nombra el fallo (only one case) y pide una prueba mejor con so we need more evidence.

prompt.es: ¿Qué argumento falla porque el hablante ataca a una persona?

choices.text: He takes one meal as a rule.
He attacks Mia instead of her point.
He mixes up a coincidence and a cause.

feedback.es: El hablante dice que Mia es una mala cocinera en lugar de responder a lo que dice sobre la comida: es un ataque personal.

origin.text: Mia says the school lunch is bad. But Mia is a terrible cook, so ignore her.

prompt.es: ¿Qué réplica es razonable ante el argumento sobre el nuevo profesor?

choices.text: You are not a teacher, so you cannot say that.
All teachers are the same, so nothing matters.
Grades may have gone down for other reasons; do you have evidence?

feedback.es: Ante una falsa causa, una réplica razonable duda de la relación y pide pruebas; las otras respuestas atacan o generalizan.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué responde Sara.

She agrees that Carlos is wrong.
She thinks homework is too long.

prompt.es: Completa la etiqueta de cada fallo.

answer.text: cause | generalisation | attack

feedback.es: Cada fallo tiene su nombre: false cause, hasty generalisation y personal attack.

You are wrong because you are young. This is a personal ___.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estos argumentos es el más razonable?

choices.text: My brother prefers mornings, so everyone prefers mornings.

You prefer mornings because you are boring.

feedback.es: Usa una muestra mayor (doce estudiantes) y una conclusión prudente (most, may). Las otras generalizan desde un caso o atacan a la persona.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada nombre con su explicación.

pairs.es: la razón no respalda la tesis

feedback.es: Cada nombre describe un fallo distinto: los casos que no bastan, la causa falsa, el ataque personal y la razón que no apoya.

prompt.es: Escribe una réplica razonable: nombra el fallo y pide una prueba.

answer.text: That may be a coincidence, not a cause. Do you have any evidence?
accepted: That may be a coincidence, not a cause. Do you have any evidence?
That could be a coincidence, not a cause. Can you show any evidence?
That may be a coincidence, not a cause. Can you show me any evidence?

feedback.es: La réplica nombra el fallo (una casualidad, no una causa) y pide una prueba sin atacar a la persona.

es: Escribir un párrafo a dos voces sobre los deberes con tesis, razón con ejemplo, contraargumento, concesión y réplica.

teaching.en: Critics say that homework helps students practise, and I admit that some of it is useful.
teaching.es: Los críticos dicen que los deberes ayudan a practicar, y reconozco que algunos son útiles.
teaching.explanationEs: Critics say = presenta el contraargumento; I admit = reconoce lo válido.
segments: Critics say that homework helps students practise, and
I admit that some of it is useful.
teaching.audioText: Critics say that homework helps students practise, and I admit that some of it is useful.

teaching.en: Although some homework is useful, too much of it leaves no time to rest.
teaching.es: Aunque algunos deberes son útiles, demasiados no dejan tiempo para descansar.
teaching.explanationEs: Although + oración completa. No se pone but en la segunda parte.
segments: Although some homework is useful, too much
of it leaves no time to rest.
teaching.audioText: Although some homework is useful, too much of it leaves no time to rest.

teaching.en: It is true that practice matters; nevertheless, a short task can teach as much as a long one.
teaching.es: Es cierto que practicar importa; sin embargo, una tarea corta puede enseñar tanto como una larga.
teaching.explanationEs: Nevertheless = sin embargo; va después de punto y coma o de punto, con una coma detrás.
segments: It is true that practice matters; nevertheless, a short
task can teach as much as a long one.
teaching.audioText: It is true that practice matters; nevertheless, a short task can teach as much as a long one.

teaching.en: A counterargument is the best point of the other side, and a rebuttal answers it.
teaching.es: Un contraargumento es el mejor punto de la otra parte, y una réplica lo responde.
teaching.explanationEs: Counterargument = lo que diría la otra parte; rebuttal = tu respuesta a eso.
segments: A counterargument is the best point of the
other side, and a rebuttal answers it.
teaching.audioText: A counterargument is the best point of the other side, and a rebuttal answers it.

teaching.en: Some teachers give ten tasks, whereas others give only two.
teaching.es: Algunos profesores ponen diez tareas, mientras que otros ponen solo dos.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereas contrasta dos hechos; en español equivale a «mientras que».
segments: Some teachers give ten tasks,
whereas others give only two.
teaching.audioText: Some teachers give ten tasks, whereas others give only two.

teaching.en: Admit what is valid in the other view, then show why your claim is still stronger.
teaching.es: Reconoce lo que es válido en la otra postura y después muestra por qué tu tesis sigue siendo más fuerte.
teaching.explanationEs: Valid = correcto o razonable; admitirlo hace tu argumento más creíble.
segments: Admit what is valid in the other view,
then show why your claim is still stronger.
teaching.audioText: Admit what is valid in the other view, then show why your claim is still stronger.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase introduce un contraargumento?

choices.text: My claim is that homework should be shorter.
Some parents say that homework builds good habits.
For example, Leo has three tasks every night.

feedback.es: El contraargumento recoge lo que diría la otra parte (Some parents say…); las otras frases son la tesis y un ejemplo.

hint.es: El contraargumento es lo que diría la otra parte.

prompt.es: Completa: «Aunque los deberes son útiles, quitan tiempo de descanso.»

answer.text: Although

answer.text: Homework should be shorter. Many students sleep only six hours on school nights, and tired students learn badly. For example, Leo finishes his tasks at eleven and cannot follow the first lesson. Mia has the same problem, and she misses her sports club twice a week. Critics say that homework helps students practise. I admit that some practice is useful, and a short task can help a lot. However, three hours of tasks every night is too much. Although practice matters, rest matters too, because a rested student remembers more in class. Nevertheless, teachers can still give useful tasks if they keep them short. A task of twenty minutes can teach the same idea. Therefore, schools should limit homework to one hour a day.
accepted: Homework should be shorter. Many students sleep only six hours on school nights, and tired students learn badly. Although practice matters, rest matters too, because a rested student remembers more in class. Nevertheless, teachers can still give useful tasks if they keep them short. A task of twenty minutes can teach the same idea. Therefore, schools should limit homework to one hour a day.

Homework should be shorter. Many students sleep only six hours during the week, so they are tired in class. For instance, Tom finishes his tasks very late and cannot listen to the lesson the next morning. Some people argue that homework helps students practise. It is true that practice is useful, and a short task can be very helpful. However, long homework every night does not give students time to rest. Although practice matters, a rested student remembers more of the lesson. Nevertheless, teachers can still give useful work if they keep it short, because twenty minutes can be enough. In conclusion, schools should limit homework to one hour a day.

answer.text: I believe that phones should stay in bags during lessons. First, phones distract students. In a school survey, 40 of 60 students said that they look at their phones in class without permission. Moreover, a clear policy helps teachers, seeing that they do not have to stop the lesson every time a phone rings. Critics say that a phone is useful in an emergency. I admit that this is a valid point. However, the school office can call the parents quickly, so students do not need a phone in the classroom. Overall, the benefit is small compared with the distraction, so the school should keep the policy.
accepted: I believe that phones should stay in bags during lessons. First, phones distract students. In a school survey, 40 of 60 students said that they look at their phones in class without permission. Moreover, a clear policy helps teachers, seeing that they do not have to stop the lesson every time a phone rings. Critics say that a phone is useful in an emergency. I admit that this is a valid point. However, the school office can call the parents quickly, so students do not need a phone in the classroom. Overall, the benefit is small compared with the distraction, so the school should keep the policy.

In my view, phones should stay in bags during lessons. The first reason is that phones distract students. According to a school survey, 40 of 60 students look at their phones in class without permission. Moreover, a clear policy helps teachers because they do not have to stop the lesson. Some people say that a phone is useful in an emergency. It is true that this can happen. Nevertheless, the school office can call the parents quickly, so a phone in the classroom is not necessary. Overall, the benefit is small compared with the distraction, and therefore the school should keep the policy.
